messages.subject: Correct way to monitoring.-
parts:
Hello!

I'm reproducing some models of chapter 17 of the ARM book, particularly that related with correlated random effects. I have been using the code here.

The main interest is in the a, b, mu_a, mu_b, sigma_a, sigma_b and rho parameters, so I would like to know the correct way to monitor the elements that have been defined in the model block.

For the moment, I use

generated quantities{

  real mu_a;
  real mu_b;
  vector[J] a;
  vector[J] b;
  matrix[J,2] B_raw_hat;
  matrix[2,2] Sigma_b_raw;
  matrix[J,2] B_raw;
  real sigma_a;
  real sigma_b;
  real rho;

  mu_a = xi_a * mu_a_raw;
  mu_b = xi_b * mu_b_raw;

  Sigma_b_raw = inverse(Tau_b_raw);

  for (j in 1:J) {
    B_raw_hat[j,1] = mu_a_raw;
    B_raw_hat[j,2] = mu_b_raw;
    # B_raw_temp ~ multi_normal(transpose(row(B_raw_hat,j)), Sigma_b_raw);
    B_raw[j,1] = B_raw_temp[1];
    B_raw[j,2] = B_raw_temp[2];
    a[j] = xi_a * B_raw[j,1];
    b[j] = xi_b * B_raw[j,2];
  }

  sigma_a = xi_a * sqrt(Sigma_b_raw[1,1]);
  sigma_b = xi_b * sqrt(Sigma_b_raw[2,2]);
  rho = Sigma_b_raw[1,2] / sqrt(Sigma_b_raw[1,1] * Sigma_b_raw[2,2]);

}

appended to the aforementioned code, but I'm not sure if this is Ok or if there exist another way.

Thanks in advance!​

What do you mean by "monitor"?

​Thanks for your answer! Well, I want to have a summary of the quantities a, b, mu_a, mu_b, sigma_a, sigma_b and rho​ which are not reported in the output of the model, at least directly. I have read this is because they are defined (or must I say declared?) in the model block. So, to obtain summary statistics about those parameters, I have been using the appended code in the previous reply, but I'm not sure if this is the correct manner to do it.

With monitoring, I also mean 'to have the posterior draws' (please excuse the ambicious meaning).

​Thanks!​

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Correct way to monitoring.-
parts:
If you want the output of those intermediate values saved then
you’ll have to define them in the transformed parameters block.
Recall that anything defined in the transformed parameters block
is available in the model block so you won’t have to recalculate
them.
